targets.claim: Kanye West settled a lawsuit with a paparazzi photographer he assaulted in 2013.
The photographer's name is Daniel Ramos.
Ramos sued West for damages and accused him of interfering with his right to pursue a lawful occupation.
West apologized to Ramos and the two shook hands, captured in a photo.
The photo of the handshake was released by Ramos' lawyer, Gloria Allred.
West pleaded no contest to a misdemeanor count of battery.
West received two years' probation and community service.
Allred stated the case sent an important message that celebrities are not above the law and cannot physically attack someone simply because they were asked a question.

claims.quote: Kanye West has settled a lawsuit with a paparazzi photographer he assaulted in 2013.
claims.reason: The evidence confirms West settled a civil lawsuit with photographer Daniel Ramos over an assault that occurred in July 2013.
claims.evidence_quote: Kanye West has settled a lawsuit with a paparazzi photographer he assaulted

claims.quote: The photographer, Daniel Ramos, had sued West for damages and accused him of interfering with his right to pursue a lawful occupation.
claims.reason: The evidence confirms Ramos filed a civil suit seeking general and punitive damages and alleging West interfered with his right to pursue a lawful occupation.
claims.evidence_quote: Ramos and his lawyer, Gloria Allred, sought general and punitive damages in the civil suit, saying that West had interfered with the photographer's rights to pursue a lawful occupation.

claims.quote: Ramos accepted an apology from West and the two shook hands in a photo released by Ramos' lawyer, Gloria Allred.
claims.reason: The evidence confirms West apologized to Ramos, they shook hands, and Allred released a photo of the handshake.
claims.evidence_quote: one important aspect of it was an apology by Kanye West to our client, Daniel Ramos... Her statement included a picture of West and Ramos shaking hands, which she said happened after the apology.

claims.quote: Ramos and West had previously reached a criminal settlement in which West pleaded no contest to a misdemeanor count of battery and received two years' probation and community service.
claims.reason: The evidence describes a criminal case where West pleaded no contest and was sentenced by a judge — not a 'criminal settlement.' The evidence does not characterize the criminal proceeding as a settlement.
claims.evidence_quote: West pleaded no contest last year to a misdemeanor count of battery over the scuffle. A judge sentenced him to two years' probation, as well as anger management sessions and community service.

claims.quote: Allred stated that the case sent an important message that celebrities are not above the law and cannot physically attack someone simply because they were asked a question.
claims.reason: The evidence directly quotes Allred making this statement.
claims.evidence_quote: "We believe that this case sent an important message," Allred said. "Celebrities are not above the law, and they have no right to physically attack someone simply because they were asked a question."
